item.title: Park Conversations: Remembering and Honoring the Soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment
item.description:
Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Clay Family Eastern Glades, 6500 Memorial Dr, Houston, TX, 77007, United States

Join us for a free audio story exhibit at Clay Family Eastern Glades Beginning August 20, Memorial Park Conservancy and the Buffalo Soldiers National Museum invite the public to Clay Family Eastern Glades for the annual return of our historic interactive audio installation, Park Conversations: Remembering and Honoring the Soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment. The exhibit will be available to experience on-site through September 27. Can’t make it to the exhibit? All stories are available online. Click Here to learn more and listen now. The history of Memorial Park and Camp Logan Before Memorial Park, the land was Camp Logan – a U.S. Army training camp built in the spring of 1917, just weeks after the United States entered World War I. That summer, African American soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, one of the Army’s four “Buffalo Soldiers” regiments, arrived to guard the camp’s construction. In the aftermath of the tragedy on August 23, 1917, the battalion was disarmed and transferred. What followed was the largest court-martial in American military history, resulting in the execution of 19 soldiers and life sentences for 63 others. That verdict stood until November 13, 2023, when the U.S. Army formally set aside the convictions of all 110 soldierstried in the case. The Army also committed to correcting the soldiers’ service records, making their descendants eligible for benefits their families had been denied for a century.   Exhibit Details: Presented in partnership with the Buffalo Soldiers National Museum, the installation uses onsite audio stories to bring this history to life throughout Clay Family Eastern Glades. Where: Clay Family Eastern Glades, 552 East Memorial Loop Drive, Houston, TX 77007 When: August 20 – September 27 Cost: Free and open to the public Bring headphones. The audio is designed for personal, uninterrupted listening Parking: Paid parking available onsite at a rate of $2 for 3 hours. Free parking is available in adjacent lots.

Amazing ArachnidsOctober 10 Spiders are so much more than Halloween decorations. They fill the role of pest control specialist in our ecosystem. Want to learn more about these amazing arachnids? Then get into the Halloween spirit by learning more about spiders. Fall FoliageNovember 7 Although Houston is not known for its fall colors, there are still lots to learn about leaves! Join us and learn more about the difference between the two and why leaves are important in the fall. Animal HomesDecember 5 There is no central heating outdoors, so where do the animals go when they get cold? To their homes, of course! Burrows, leaves, nests, and so much more. Find out all the different types of animal homes and who lives in what.

Hermann Park Conservancy’s 12th annual Park to Port Bike Ride is set for Saturday, October 24. The 20-mile round-trip bike ride takes cyclists from Hermann Park’s Bayou Parkland along the Bayou Greenway trail all the way to Mason Park, near the Port of Houston.
